Fixed. The bug was in `paths.PathEscape` (common/paths/path.go:377), used to build `TargetPaths.Link` (resources/page/page_paths.go:276). It parsed the link with `url.Parse`, which treated `#` as a fragment delimiter, so `EscapedPath()` returned everything before it — truncating `/posts/2024/04/newsletter-#4/` to `/posts/2024/04/newsletter-`.

The fix pre-escapes `#` as `%23` before parsing; already-escaped `%23` sequences pass through unchanged (no double-escaping), and `EscapedPath()` keeps the encoding.

Verified:
- `paths.PathEscape("/posts/2024/04/newsletter-#4/index.html")` now returns `/posts/2024/04/newsletter-%234/index.html` (previously `/posts/2024/04/newsletter-`)
- `go test ./common/... ./resources/... ./helpers/ ./tpl/urls/` all pass (an end-to-end hugolib run wasn't possible offline due to missing test-module downloads)
